html:
The eruption of the volcanic island of Krakatoa, in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, which climaxed on 27 August 1883. It was one of the deadliest and most destructive eruptions in recorded history.

The volcano had been active since May. On 27 August a series of huge explosions destroyed most of the island, which collapsed into a sea filled crater. The sound was heard thousands of kilometres away, as far as Australia and islands of the Indian Ocean. Tsunamis up to 30 metres high swept the coasts of west Java and south Sumatra, then part of the Dutch East Indies, and killed most of the more than 36,000 people who died.

Ash and gas spread around the world. Average temperatures fell for several years, and skies glowed red at sunset in Europe and America. Because the news went out by telegraph, it was the first great natural disaster the whole world followed almost as it happened. A new volcano, Anak Krakatau, rose from the sea in 1927. Compare the even larger Tambora eruption of 1815 and New Zealand's Tarawera eruption three years later.
sum: The eruption of the volcanic island of Krakatoa, in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, which climaxed on 27 August 1883. It was one of the deadliest and most destructive eruptions in recorded history.
